channel.title: BusinessHub.cy — SME
channel.description: Latest SME stories from BusinessHub.cy, Cyprus Edition.

item.title: Vulnerability profiles of least developed countries
item.description: UNCTAD has released updated vulnerability profiles for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) to assess their readiness for graduation from the LDC category.

item.title: Opening Keynote Address of the Chief Scientist for Research, Innovation and Technology of the Republic of Cyprus, Dr Demetris Skourides, at the 10th PMI Cyprus Chapter Project Management Conference
item.description: Chief Scientist Demetris Skourides calls for a paradigm shift in Cyprus's project management, emphasizing the integration of AI to move from execution to 'intelligent execution.'

item.title: Real household income in the OECD contracts slightly in Q2 2026
item.description: OECD real household income per capita edged down 0.1% in Q2 2026, as persistent inflation began outpacing nominal wage gains despite continued GDP growth.

item.title: OEB: Award Ceremony of the Cyprus Innovation Awards of the OEB and the Cyprus Research Awards of the RIF
item.description: OEB and RIF will host the joint 19th Cyprus Innovation and Research Awards on October 26, 2026, to honor excellence in business innovation and scientific research.

item.title: Choosing Growth: Reforms for Innovation, Scale, and Resilience
item.description: The IMF warns Europe to prioritize fiscal consolidation and structural reforms to counter rising sovereign yields, energy shocks, and stagnant growth.

item.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2026 Article IV Consultation and Mid-Term Review and Request for Reduction of Access under Flexible Credit Line Arrangement with Mexico
item.description: The IMF approved Mexico's credit line reduction following improved economic stability, while advising tighter fiscal policies to manage debt and inflation despite a projected growth recovery through 2027.

item.title: Finland: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2027 Article IV Mission
item.description: Finland's economy enters a recovery phase driven by exports and investment, though high unemployment and fiscal deficits necessitate structural reforms and consolidation.

item.title: IMF Staff Concludes Visit to Georgia
item.description: The IMF reports robust 7.2% growth for Georgia in 2026 driven by ICT and trade, while warning that persistent inflation may necessitate tighter monetary policy.

item.title: IMF Staff Completes 2026 Article IV Mission to Vietnam
item.description: Vietnam's economy is projected to grow by 9.2% in 2026, driven by AI and tech, though inflation risks and trade uncertainties remain for international partners.

item.title: Creating the Conditions for Lasting Diversification in Algeria
item.description: Algeria is intensifying efforts to diversify its economy away from hydrocarbons through large-scale infrastructure projects and regulatory reforms to stimulate private sector growth.

item.title: Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting Plenary Meeting Opening, remarks by OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann
item.description: OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann highlights the global implementation of the 15% minimum tax and outlines future priorities for international tax cooperation and profit-shifting prevention.

item.title: OECD unemployment rate stable at 5.0% in September 2026, while youth unemployment rate reaches 11.5%
item.description: The OECD unemployment rate held steady at 5.0% in September 2026, though youth unemployment rose to 11.5% and gender gaps persisted in Greece and the Eurozone.

item.title: Government support to agriculture grew by 15% in the last two years and much of it is distortive, says OECD
item.description: Global agricultural support rose 15% to $885 billion, largely through distortive subsidies that risk long-term productivity and increase consumer costs, according to the OECD.

item.title: Reforms can strengthen Belgium’s competitiveness, unlock its growth potential and support sustainable public finances
item.description: The OECD urges Belgium to implement structural reforms in wage-setting, public spending, and green energy to address rising debt and slowing GDP growth.

item.title: Rising exposure to extreme heat and droughts poses growing risks to economies, OECD finds
item.description: The OECD reports a massive global increase in extreme heat and a decline in soil moisture, threatening agricultural stability, energy production, and international supply chains.

item.title: Migration to OECD countries declines for second consecutive year, but remains high by historical standards
item.description: OECD migration fell 1.6% in 2025 to 6.1 million, but remains historically high, highlighting the critical need for better skill utilization to drive productivity amidst labor shortages.

item.title: Large enterprises led EU services exports in 2024
item.description: Eurostat data reveals that large enterprises continue to dominate EU services exports, underscoring the competitive gap facing SMEs in international markets.

item.title: Welcome Speech by the Shipping Deputy Minister of the Republic of Cyprus, Ms Marina Hadjimanolis,...
item.description: Island Energies (formerly Island Oil) has rebranded to reflect its international expansion and commitment to sustainable maritime services and strategic growth within the Cyprus shipping cluster.

item.title: EIB Group boosts support for Ukrainian businesses with EU-backed guarantees and grants
item.description: The EIB Group and EU have launched €286 million in guarantees and grants to support over 2,200 Ukrainian SMEs via local banks.

item.title: Agenda: Committee on Financial and Budgetary Affairs - Meeting 16/11/2026 - REVISED
item.description: The Cyprus House Finance Committee has scheduled a revised legislative meeting for November 16, 2026, to discuss critical budgetary and economic matters.

item.title: Agenda: Committee on Financial and Budgetary Affairs - Session 13/11/2026
item.description: The Cyprus House of Representatives has scheduled key committee sessions for mid-November 2026, focusing on finance, trade, and human rights.

item.title: Dutch Biotech fighting ALS and other neuro-degenerative diseases gets European backing
item.description: The EIB is providing a €30 million loan to VectorY Therapeutics to advance vectorised antibody treatments for neurodegenerative diseases like ALS and Alzheimer's under the InvestEU programme.

item.title: State Employees by Category - Total Employment: 55.317 (Oct 2026)
item.description: Total employment in the Cyprus public sector reached 55,317 in October 2026, signaling a growing state footprint in the labor market.

item.title: Registration Of Motor Vehicles: January–October 2026
item.description: Cyprus motor vehicle registrations rose 8.7% in Jan-Oct 2026, driven by a significant shift toward hybrid saloon cars and increased demand for heavy goods vehicles.

item.title: President of the Republic of Cyprus – Delegations from CCOD, CyFPA and Cyprus Third Age Observatory
item.description: President Christodoulides met with key civil society organizations focusing on human rights, family planning, and elderly care to discuss social policy and community support.

item.title: Government Spokesman – Media briefing
item.description: The Government Spokesman conducted a scheduled media briefing at the Presidential Palace to update the press on current executive affairs and government priorities.

item.title: Address by the Commissioner for the Environment and Animal Welfare of the Republic of Cyprus, Mr ...
item.description: Cyprus' Environment Commissioner advocates for the adoption of the SUSEDI sustainability framework across public and private sectors to align operations with green transition goals.

item.title: Keynote Address by the Minister of Health of the Republic of Cyprus, Mr Neophytos Charalambides, ...
item.description: Cyprus Health Minister emphasizes that national health resilience depends on digital security, supply chain autonomy, and European-level cooperation to mitigate regional and logistical vulnerabilities.

item.title: Building Permits - Decrease of 3,0% in the Number of Building Permits Jul 2026
item.description: Cyprus building permits dropped by 3.0% in July 2026, indicating a potential slowdown in upcoming construction activity and real estate supply.

item.title: Slovak region Banská Bystrica to upgrade infrastructure with €20 million EIB loan and €5 million EU grant
item.description: Slovakia’s Banská Bystrica region receives €25 million in EIB and EU funding for 100 infrastructure projects under the Just Transition Mechanism.

item.title: Services production up by 0.3% in the euro area
item.description: Euro area services production grew by 0.3% in August 2026, driven by strong gains in information and communication, despite a slight dip in professional services and hospitality.

item.title: Latest news on EIB's support for Ukraine
item.description: The EIB has deployed over €4.5 billion since 2022 to support Ukraine's infrastructure, energy, and SMEs, with an additional €1.5 billion planned for 2025.

item.title: EIB Group Activity Report 2025: Powering Europe
item.description: The EIB Group reached a record €100 billion in financing in 2025, prioritizing European competitiveness, security, and climate resilience through strategic investments.

item.title: 2026 field season of the “Life at the Furnace” project in the Peristerona Valley, Lefkosia District
item.description: International researchers completed the 2026 'Life at the Furnace' project season, uncovering long-term settlement patterns and Roman copper production history in the Peristerona Valley.

item.title: The Minister of Finance participated in the EU Economic and Financial Affairs Council
item.description: Cyprus supports EU tobacco tax modernization and simplification of business regulations at ECOFIN, emphasizing balanced fiscal policy and defense investment.

item.title: Foreign Trade Statistics - Sep 2026 (Provisional Data) and Aug 2026 (Final Data)
item.description: Cyprus trade deficit widens in late 2026, driven by rising imports and volatile export performance according to latest provisional and final data from Cystat.

item.title: LABOUR MARKET INDICATORS
item.description: Cyprus labor market indicators show record-high employment and a significant drop in unemployment, alongside a steady rise in average monthly earnings through 2025 forecasts.

item.description: The Cyprus House of Representatives has scheduled key committee sessions for early November 2026, focusing on finance, commerce, and labor.

item.title: A ‘small business act’ for European SMEs
item.description: The EU Small Business Act (SBA) establishes a framework of 10 principles to reduce bureaucracy, improve financing, and facilitate market access for SMEs across member states.

item.title: SME Relief Package - Communication from the Commission
item.description: The European Commission has launched a comprehensive SME Relief Package to provide financial support and regulatory simplification for small and medium-sized enterprises across the EU.

item.description: Cyprus retail trade saw significant growth in September 2026, with value increasing by 10.4% and volume by 7.7% compared to the previous year.

item.title: Euro area unemployment at 6.3%
item.description: Eurozone unemployment reached a historic low of 6.3% in September 2024, highlighting a persistent labor shortage across the currency union.
